output.name: Hessak

anatomy.part: the grip, the rounded knob at the end of the bone shaft
the upper bend where the shaft turns away from the grip
the middle of the long shaft
the shank's bend, where the shaft turns down into the hook
the belly of the hook, its lowest curve
the barb tip curling back up

output.myth: Kessa went out on the sea-ice one grey morning, when the wind had dropped and the ice was singing. A man had gone through near the shelves. His coat had spread out under the water like a sail. Kessa had only her bone hook and a length of gut. She lay flat and felt about with the hook until it caught in his collar. Then she pulled. He came up grey as a gutted fish and did not breathe for a long time. Then he did. Tavo laughed when he heard, as he laughs at everything he has not wrecked yet. Kael, who has cast for fallen stars since before the islands had names, said nothing. Kessa hung the hook on the sky to dry, and it is there still. Look south when the ice is moving. The hook catches the cold light and will not let it go. Some nights the drowned man's coat hangs from it, waiting to be flown.
output.verse:
Grey ice, a bone hook
catches the cold southern light
it will not let go

problems: The blind guess (boot or bird's head with beak) does not name the intended ice hook. Only the vague 'hook-shaped' part lands, so the silhouette does not read clearly as an ice hook.
The hook reads as a blunt, angular box. The shaft and hook are short relative to the outline, and the curve does not look like a pick that bends sharply down and back.
The grip (5364 at about x447, y240) is a tiny knob on the end of the shaft and barely reads as a rounded handle.
The barb tip (6670 at about x370, y317) is a short stub pointing up-right. It does not read as a barb that curls back toward the shaft.

The figure is rotated: the shaft runs horizontally across the top and the hook hangs down-left. An ice hook is normally drawn with the grip at the top of a vertical shaft, so this orientation reads oddly.

Labels collide: 'the upper bend where the shaft...' overprints 'the middle of the long shaft', and 'the belly of the hook' runs over the blue outline. The label text is also clipped at the right edge.

The blue silhouette is a real outline and not a copy of the gold lines, which is good. Stars 5799 (422,198), 8645 (260,240) and 8102 (291,340) sit on the correct corners. Star 6537 (380,203) sits on the top edge of the shaft, a little off its midpoint.
judge.advice: Redraw so the figure reads unmistakably as an ice hook. Make the shaft a long, near-straight bar running vertically, with the grip at the top: put 5364 on a clearly rounded knob at the top end (around x≈260, y≈60 in the current frame, or rotate the whole figure so the shaft is vertical). Place 5799 where the shaft turns away from the grip, slightly below the knob. Place 6537 on the midpoint of the shaft, not on the top edge. Place 8645 at the shank bend, where the shaft curves into the hook. Make the hook a deep, smooth arc so 8102 sits at its lowest point, and hook the barb 6670 back up and toward the shaft so the tip curls inward. Widen the silhouette so the hook is wider than the shaft. Move the labels to separate spots with leader lines so they do not overlap each other or the outline, and keep all text inside the frame.
